NEW DELHI: As India enter a critical phase in their bid to stay alive in the World Test Championship (WTC) race, Jasprit Bumrah and Shubman Gill are taking a cautious approach to regaining full fitness ahead of the two-Test series in Sri Lanka starting Aug 15.TOI understands that Bumrah will begin gradually increasing his bowling workload after suffering an impact injury during the ODI series in England, while Gill has sought help from specialists outside the BCCI for his chronic neck problem.It is learnt that Bumrah developed swelling in his knee before the final ODI at Lord’s on June 19 but the medical team is confident he will be ready for the first Test in Galle. The selectors picked him for the Sri Lanka tour subject to fitness. The focus is now on preparing him to endure the rigours of Test cricket.Bumrah has played little longer-format cricket since the second Test against South Africa in Guwahati last Nov. He has featured only in T20 cricket, apart from two ODIs in England last month. Bumrah is currently at the Centre of Excellence (CoE).“Bumrah will start bowling this week and his workload will be gradually increased. He needs to get used to bowling longer spells again.The medical team at CoE will be closely monitoring it, and the initial reports are that he should be good to start the first Test. These two Test matches are very important for India. Dropping even one Test here will put immense pressure on the team to qualify for the WTC final next year. That’s why the team management wants Bumrah to be available in prime shape for the series,” a BCCI source told TOI.As for Gill, it is learnt that he has been consulting specialists to address the neck pain that first flared up during his first innings in the opening Test against South Africa at Eden Gardens. The problem eventually ruled him out of the rest of the series, which India lost 0-2. He also missed an IPL match because of the recurring pain.“Gill has been battling the neck pain for some time. It flares up every now and then, especially when he bats for a longer period. He has been consulting specialists outside BCCI for treatment and he is much better now. It’s an ongoing process. India felt his absence in that South Africa series.That’s why he has taken a cautious approach in addressing the chronic issue,” the source said.Sai Sudharsan, India’s No. 3 batter in Tests, has also been selected subject to fitness. He is recovering from a hamstring injury and will resume batting at the CoE next week. The BCCI medical team has shared a positive report regarding his availability for the first Test.
Article Summary: Jasprit Bumrah will begin gradually increasing his bowling workload. Shubman Gill has sought help from specialists outside the BCCI for his chronic neck problem. India's No. 3 batter Sai Sudharsan will resume batting at the CoE next week.

Article Title: How India became the world's worst doping offender: A crisis threatening sports
Article Text:
Judoka Arun Kumar and Tulika Maan (Image credit: Agencies)

A Disturbing Trend



New Substances. Old Pattern



Beyond Punishment



Athletes Lead Message



Beyond Black & White



Education, Not Fear



Uneasy Contradiction

The Real Test



Shortly before the Commonwealth Games (CWG) began at Glasgow, a startling doping scandal rocked the weightlifting contingent. Four national campers - N Ajith (71kg), Sairaj Pardeshi (88kg), Harcharan Singh (110kg) and Vanshita Verma (77kg) - tested positive for prohibited substances during the qualification period, forcing them out of the games. The fallout extended beyond individual suspensions. Under CWG regulations, the repeated anti-doping rule violations (ADRVs) resulted in India losing a weightlifting quota, denying Dilbagh Singh a place in the squad despite earning selection on merit.There was more to follow. Men’s 73kg judoka Arun Kumar, winner of last year’s Taipei Asian Open gold medal, was provisionally suspended after testing positive for a banned anabolic steroid. Days later came perhaps the biggest setback when Olympian and Birmingham CWG silver medallist Tulika Maan (+78kg) was provisionally suspended after accumulating three whereabouts failures within a rolling 12-month period.It wasn’t just the potential loss of medals. Six high-profile anti-doping setbacks across two disciplines shifted the conversation away from podium finishes to the country’s disgraceful relationship with doping.Yet, at a time when India is the world’s worst doping offender in sports, with its credibility at its lowest ebb, few want to openly discuss the elephant in the room.But looking away doesn’t make the problem disappear. That too at a time when Ahmedabad is preparing to host the next Commonwealth Games in 2030 and the country has formally declared its intention to host the 2036 Olympics.According to the World Anti-Doping Agency’s (WADA) 2024 Testing Figures Report, released in Dec 2025, India registered 260 adverse analytical findings (AAFs) from 7,113 samples collected during the year — a positivity rate of 3.6%. Among countries conducting more than 5,000 tests annually, India recorded the highest positivity rate in the world for the third consecutive year.The comparison with other sporting powers is sobering. France reported 91 violations from 11,744 tests, Russia 76 from 10,514 samples, while China found only 43 positives despite collecting over 24,000 samples. The United States recorded a positivity rate of just 1.1% after conducting more than 6,500 tests.The challenge is visible in athletics. The Athletics Integrity Unit (AIU) currently lists India as the country with the highest number of active sanctions worldwide. As many as 162 Indian athletes and support personnel are serving bans under the AIU framework, ahead of Kenya (148) and Russia (60).The list of substances repeatedly surfacing in Indian cases reflects a worrying trend. Stanozolol, a synthetic anabolic steroid banned under WADA’s S1 category, continues to dominate anti-doping reports despite years of awareness campaigns. The drug is designed to promote muscle growth, accelerate recovery and reduce body fat.Recent athletes testing positive for stanozolol include former Youth World boxing champion Vinka, Asian Indoor rowing championships winner Gursewak Singh, junior sprint sensation Nipam Chauhan, wrestler Shubham and kabaddi player Akash Nathu Disale.Perhaps the most damaging among recent cases has been Nipam. India’s fastest junior woman sprinter now faces losing the silver and bronze medals she won at the Asian Under-20 championships in Hong Kong after testing positive for stanozolol.The govt has begun shifting its focus beyond athletes to the wider ecosystem that enables doping. At the inaugural conference of WADA’s ‘Global Anti-Doping Intelligence and Investigations Network’ (GAIIN) held recently in New Delhi, sports minister Mansukh Mandaviya outlined what could become the biggest overhaul of India’s antidoping policy.“Doping today is no longer an individual act but an organised multinational enterprise,” he said, adding that the proposed changes to the National Anti-Doping Amendment Act 2025 seek to bring coaches, doctors, suppliers and traffickers within the ambit of criminal liability.Draft provisions envisage prison terms ranging from five to 10 years, along with financial penalties for those involved in administering or trafficking banned substances. Athletes guilty only of anti-doping rule violations would continue to be dealt with under existing sporting regulations.Mandaviya underlined that India’s ambitions extend beyond medals. “India is committed not only to sporting excellence but to upholding the highest standards of integrity,” he said, adding that awareness, education and technology would remain central pillars of the nation’s clean sport programme.The govt has simultaneously expanded testing, almost doubling annual samples from around 4,000 in 2019 to nearly 8,000 over the past year. “Our testing programme has expanded significantly in recent years, complemented by a strategic shift towards risk-based and effectiveness-driven approaches. However, as we recognise, testing alone is no longer sufficient, and integration, intelligence and education must form the core of our antidoping framework,” said NADA director general Anant Kumar.Olympic and world champion Neeraj Chopra has now become one of the strongest voices advocating athlete education. After launching the ‘Clean Sport’ initiative with the Indian Olympic Association (IOA) through the Neeraj Chopra Foundation (NCF), Chopra said many athletes violate anti-doping rules because they simply lack reliable guidance.“Any doping violation is a concern because it impacts both the athlete and the sport. But not every case comes from an intention to gain unfair advantage. Sometimes athletes simply don’t know enough about what they are consuming or whom to trust for advice,” Chopra told TOI.Explaining his decision to champion the campaign despite a packed schedule, Chopra added: “Many athletes lack access to the right information on supplements, medications and anti-doping rules. Years of hard work can be put at risk by a small mistake.”Not everyone believes the present anti-doping framework is beyond criticism. Sports medicine expert Dr PSM Chandran argues that while cheating cannot be condoned, the current system also raises scientific and ethical concerns.“Doping may indeed be injurious to sport. Fair play matters, and cheating cannot be condoned. However, doping control in its present format is also injurious to athletes as it adheres rigidly to the WADA Code while often disregarding evidence-based medicine, proportionality and natural justice,” he said.He questioned whether every positive test necessarily translates into a measurable competitive advantage and called upon authorities to publish performance analyses of athletes before and after alleged doping periods.“Without such evidence, the claim that banned substances universally enhance performance remains belief, not science,” argued Chandran, president of the Indian Federation of Sports Medicine (IFSM). His views are likely to divide opinion, but they also underline the complexity of anti-doping policy, where science, ethics and sporting integrity often intersect.National gymnastics coach Manoj Rana believes India’s response must begin much earlier. “Indian sport has witnessed remarkable progress on the global stage, but the rising number of doping violations continues to tarnish these achievements. The answer is not only stricter punishments but stronger prevention,” Rana said.He points to intense pressure on athletes to win medals, secure govt employment and retain financial support, often without access to qualified nutritionists, sports scientists or evidence-based medical guidance.The problem is further complicated by changing training patterns. Many elite Indian athletes now train overseas, particularly in Eastern Europe and high-altitude centres in Russia, Turkey and Georgia. While foreign exposure has improved performances, investigators also believe some athletes operate outside India’s domestic testing ecosystem under uncertified local support personnel or littleknown foreign coaches . Indian authorities have previously terminated engagements with certain Eastern European coaches after sudden spikes in positive tests among elite campers.Ironically, at a time when India faces global scrutiny over doping, financial support for its anti-doping institutions has declined.The Union Budget reduced allocations for both NADA and National Dope Testing Laboratory (NDTL). NADA’s allocation fell from Rs 24.30 crore to Rs 20.30 crore, while the revised allocation for NDTL dropped from Rs 28.55 crore to Rs 23 crore, with the laboratory’s own budget reduced to Rs 5.55 crore.The cuts inevitably raise questions over whether India’s antidoping institutions can continue expanding testing, intelligence gathering and education precisely when they are needed most.For India, therefore, Glasgow represents far more than another CWG. It is a reminder that hosting the CWG in Ahmedabad, securing the 2036 Olympics or staging the Asian Games in 2038 will ultimately depend not only on worldclass stadiums or impressive medal tallies, but on the credibility of the country’s sporting ecosystem.India has already demonstrated that it possesses the ambition, infrastructure and organisational capacity to emerge as a global sporting destination. But as the list of errant athletes continues to rapidly grow, the greater challenge is to provide a robust culture of clean sport. The danger of letting matters drift cannot be understated. Let us not forget that Russia was banned from international sports due to doping offences. A strict law is welcome. But authorities should also take a holistic and long-term view of the menace and find ways to fully eradicate it.
Article Summary: Six high-profile anti-doping setbacks across two disciplines shifted the conversation away from podium finishes to the country’s disgraceful relationship with doping. The Athletics Integrity Unit (AIU) currently lists India as the country with the highest number of active sanctions worldwide. As many as 162 Indian athletes and support personnel are serving bans.

Article Title: CWG 2026: Indian boxers shatter Birmingham record, guarantee 10 medals in Glasgow
Article Text:

Jaismine secures another medal



Sakshi dominates with smart tactics



Arundhati stays composed in physical contest



Sachin and Ankush cruise, Berwal battles through

NEW DELHI: India's boxers continued their impressive run at the Commonwealth Games 2026, with six more pugilists reaching the semifinals on Wednesday. The results took India's assured boxing medal tally to 10, already bettering the seven medals the country won at the 2022 Birmingham Games. Sakshi Chaudhary (51kg), Arundhati Choudhary (70kg), Sachin Siwach (60kg), Ankush Panghal (80kg), Narender Berwal (+90kg) and world champion Jaismine Lamboria (57kg) joined Lovlina Borgohain (75kg), Priya Ghanghas (60kg), Preeti Pawar (54kg) and Jadumani Singh (55kg) in the semifinals of their respective weight categories.India had finished with seven boxing medals in Birmingham - three gold, one silver and three bronze.With 10 boxers now in the last four, the country is guaranteed at least 10 bronze medals in Glasgow.In the final bout of the day, Jaismine Lamboria defeated England's Elise Glynn 4-1 in the women's 57kg quarterfinal to book her place in the semifinals.The contest was closely fought, with both boxers exchanging punches throughout. However, Jaismine's quick movement and solid defence helped her stay ahead. After a tight start, the Indian southpaw finished strongly to seal the victory.The win also ensured that Jaismine will at least match the bronze medal she won at the 2022 Commonwealth Games.Sakshi Chaudhary outclassed Northern Ireland's Caitlin Fryers with a one-sided 5-0 victory.Using her height and reach advantage after moving down from the 54kg category, Sakshi controlled the bout with sharp jabs and straight punches.Fryers tried to make the contest physical by forcing frequent clinches, and both boxers even fell to the canvas during one exchange. But Sakshi stayed calm, used her footwork well and comfortably secured the win.Arundhati Choudhary had a much tougher challenge against New Zealand's Morgan Henderson but came through with a 3-1 win.The New Zealander made the fight physical by constantly pushing, wrestling and tying up the Indian boxer. Arundhati, however, kept her composure and landed the cleaner punches whenever she had the chance.Her patience and smart boxing helped her book a place in the semifinals.Former world youth champion Sachin Siwach, one of India's strongest gold medal hopes, defeated Botswana's Treasure Moremi 5-0.After a cautious start, Sachin took complete control with clean hooks, sharp counters and better timing.Ankush Panghal also registered a comfortable 5-0 victory over Seychelles' Jade Micock. His sharp combinations and disciplined defence gave his opponent little chance, with all five judges scoring the contest in his favour.Heavyweight boxer Narender Berwal had the toughest fight of the day as he edged Samoa's Michael Seko 3-2 in a hard-fought quarterfinal.The bout saw several referee interventions, and Berwal even received two point deductions. Despite the setbacks, he forced two standing counts on his opponent, including one in the final round, to seal a narrow victory.
Article Summary: Sakshi Chaudhary, Arundhati Choudhary and Sachin Siwach reach semifinals. Ankush Panghal, Narender Berwal and world champion Jaismine Lamboria also reach last four. Results take India's assured boxing medal tally to 10, bettering the seven medals the country won at the 2022 Birmingham Games.

Article Title: Spiker-turned-goalkeeper Mohith eyes FIH World Cup splash
Article Text:
Goalkeeper HS Mohith (Image credit: Instagram)

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

BENGALURU: What began as an unwilling stint between the posts has turned into a calling. Young goalkeeper HS Mohith is now determined to impress at the upcoming FIH World Cup. If not under the bar, Mohith would have well been spiking or blocking the ball on a volleyball court.A shortage of goalkeepers at sports hostel in Hassan prompted the coach to ‘borrow’ Mohith from the volleyball team. Incidentally, the team did well in that tournament, and with his height being a disadvantage, Mohith was asked to continue with hockey.It took him barely two years to fall in love with the sport. Accepting his position, however, took longer. “I thought goalkeeping was a tough job. I went up to the coach and said I don’t want to be a goalkeeper, I want to be in forward line and score goals. It didn’t take him long to remind me that I was picked for the position and it would take them a while to train another goalkeeper,” Mohith told TOI during the World Cup preparatory camp at SAI Centre here.Disappointed but not defeated, the 24-yearold soon began looking at the role differently. “I realised how important a goalkeeper is. Unlike outfield players, who can sometimes get away with mistakes, a goalkeeper has nowhere to hide.I thrive under pressure and I started enjoying that responsibility,” he recalled.Mohith’s rise has been steady. A key member of India’s title-winning side at the 2023 Junior Asia Cup, he announced himself at last year’s Sultan Azlan Shah Cup before producing a composed display against Australia in the FIH Pro League, where he won the shootout for India.
Article Summary: Goalkeeper HS Mohith is now determined to impress at the upcoming FIH World Cup. A shortage of goalkeepers at sports hostel in Hassan prompted the coach to 'borrow' Mohith from the volleyball team. It took him barely two years to fall in love with the sport.

Article Title: Boxers pack a medal punch: Six Indians reach semifinals, assure record 10 medals
Article Text:
Sakshi Chaudhary

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

India’s medal tally is set to swell. After the weightlifters did their bit, on Wednesday it was the boxers’ turn to take centre stage at the Commonwealth Games in Glasgow.So far, 10 Indian boxers have reached their respective semifinals, assuring themselves of at least a bronze medal each. Lovlina Borgohain had made the last four of the women’s 75kg category after receiving a bye in the draw, while Priya Ghanghas (60kg), Preeti Pawar (54kg) and Jadumani Singh (55kg) won their quarterfinal bouts on Tuesday.Boxing awards two bronze medals in each category, meaning every semifinalist is guaranteed a place on the podium.Wednesday, however, brought a six-medal windfall, beginning with Sakshi Chaudhary, who faced European Championships silver medallist Caitlin Fryers of Northern Ireland in the women’s 51kg quarterfinal. Fryers charged forward from the opening bell but Sakshi refused to be overpowered. She used her footwork well, landing clean punches before moving out of range to seal a 5-0 unanimous-decision victory.In the next bout, it was Arundhati Choudhary’s turn to shine in the women’s 70kg category. The first woman boxer from Rajasthan to compete at the CWG ensured she would not leave Glasgow empty-handed, although the contest was tougher than she may have anticipated.Her opponent, New Zealand’s Morgan Henderson, used to play rugby, and that aggression was evident in the ring. Henderson was docked a point but Arundhati matched her intensity and made the cleaner punches count to claim a 3-1 split-decision victory.In the men’s 60kg quarterfinal, world No. 5 and former World Youth champion Sachin Siwach registered a dominant 5-0 win over Botswana’s Treasure Moremi. In the men’s 80kg quarterfinal, Ankush Yadav advanced with a 5-0 unanimous-decision victory over Seychelles’ Jade Micock, while Narender Berwal completed the sweep by edging Samoa’s Michael Seko 3-2 in the men’s 90kg-plus quarterfinal.Later in the evening, Jaismine advanced to the women’s 57kg semifinals with 4-1 a win over Elise Glynn of England.India enjoyed a good day in the field too, with Tajinderpal Singh Toor and Samardeep Singh Gill progressing to the men’s shot put final. National record-holder Toor opened with 19.93m in Group A before improving to 20.14m to breach the automatic qualification mark of 20m. The twotime Asian Games champion then opted against taking his third throw.Gill qualified with his best throw of 19.95m in his first attempt in Group B. He followed it with 19.75m before fouling his third and final attempt.There was, however, disappointment in the women’s high jump final, where Asian U20 champion and national record-holder Pooja Singh finished eighth. She cleared 1.77m on her second attempt but failed to clear 1.82m. Weightlifter Sanjana Panchal was also eliminated early after failing all three snatch attempts at her opening weight of 94kg in the women’s 77kg event.
Article Summary: 10 Indian boxers have reached their respective semifinals, assuring themselves of at least a bronze medal each. Sakshi Chaudhary beat Caitlin Fryers of Northern Ireland in the women’s 51kg quarterfinal. Arundhati Choudhary won 3-1 split-decision over Morgan Henderson of New Zealand. Tajinderpal Singh Toor and Samardeep Singh Gill progressed to the men�'s shot put final.

Article Title: CWG 2026: Indian boxers unfazed by baggage snag on arrival
Article Text:
Santiago Nieva (Image credit: X)

India’s boxing contingent arrived in Glasgow confident after a productive two-week multinational training camp in Belfast, but its final preparations were briefly disrupted when some boxers’ luggage failed to arrive ahead of Thursday’s opening ceremony.The 14-member squad travelled from Belfast to Glasgow on Tuesday after completing the intensive camp, during which the boxers benefitted from quality sparring and competition-specific training. However, several athletes were left without their bags, which also contained their ceremonial outfits, TOI has learnt.Sources said officials from the Indian Olympic Association (IOA) and the chef-de-mission’s office were at the airport on Wednesday, coordinating with the airline to ensure the baggage reached the contingent before the ceremony. The boxing competition begins on Friday and runs until Aug 1.The incident, however, has not gone down well with the Boxing Federation of India (BFI). Sources said that after the issue surfaced, the federation asked the boxers to submit declarations stating that they would not speak to the media about internal team matters and would instead remain focused on their performances.Despite the logistical hiccup, the mood in the camp remains upbeat. “We are settling in well in Glasgow. We had a good camp in Belfast where everybody got quality sparring and proper preparations. The boxers are managing their weights well. We will have the draws soon. We are coming with high expectations for this competition,” India women’s head coach Santiago Nieva told TOI .India’s 14-member squad features Olympic bronze medallist Lovlina Borgohain and Jaismine Lamboria, the world No. 1 in the women’s 57kg category.
Article Summary: India’s boxing contingent arrived in Glasgow confident after a productive two- week multinational training camp in Belfast. The 14-member squad travelled from Belfast to Glasgow on Tuesday after completing the intensive camp. Article Title: CWG 2026: Glasgow show puts Asian Games qualification setback in shade
Article Text:
Gulveer Singh (Image credit: X)

KNOW GULVEER | Age 28



Born in Sirsa village, Aligarh (UP)

Naib Subedar in the Grenadiers regiment of the Indian Army

Training base Colorado Springs, USA

Coach Scott Simmons

Favoured events 5,000m & 10,000m

Became first-ever Indian athlete to complete a half-marathon in under 60 minutes (59:42)

Clocked 3:55.63 at the Music City Track Carnival in the USA to become the first Indian runner to break the four-minute mile barrier

Won bronze in the 10,000m at the Asian Games in 2022

Won gold in the 5,000 & 10,000 at the Asian Athletics Championships in 2025

NEW DELHI: For Gulveer Singh, spending months away from home, missing the birth of his daughter and banking solely on video calls to his family were sacrifices that found a sweet reward as the 28-year-old clinched Commonwealth Games silver.“It has been six to eight months since I got home. It’s a lonely world out there for me. I can only see the face of my child during video calls. But to represent the nation is equally important,” Gulveer had said prior to his departure.The road to Glasgow wasn’t smooth. Ankle and knee sprains disrupted preparations while the Athletics Federation of India (AFI) asked him to return from his overseas base to compete at the InterState championships and prove his fitness. On his return, although he fell short of the upcoming Asian Games qualifying mark, Gulveer and coach Scott Simmons persisted with their programme at Colorado Springs, gradually rebuilding fitness and improving his timings. The dip in form in the lead up to the CWG caused concern, but Gulveer trained hard for the event.“I only focus on giving my best. I worked on improving my fitness and timing. Also, I don’t keep track of my national records and all,” he had said.Before joining the 23 Grenadiers in 2018, Gulveer had never dreamt of becoming an international athlete. “I started running seriously after joining the Army. Before that, I used to run only to get enrolled. I didn’t know anything about the CWG or Asian Games. I only came to know about them after joining the Army. ”His life changed almost accidentally in 2019. Stationed in Arunachal Pradesh, Gulveer prepared seriously for an inter-unit cross-country race, hoping a good performance would earn incentives and provide respite from demanding military duties. His 10km victory in 30:58 caught the eye of Army Sports Institute coach Younus Khan, who brought him to Pune and transformed a soldier into India’s premier distance runner.That mindset was evident in Glasgow. Amid rain, the reigning Asian 5,000m and 10,000m champion judged the pace superbly, adding another medal to a kitty that already boast of an Asian Games bronze and Asian Championship double gold.
Article Summary: Gulveer Singh won silver at the Commonwealth Games in Glasgow. The 28-year-old became the first Indian runner to break the four-minute mile barrier. The reigning Asian 5,000m and 10,000M champion judged the pace superbly.

Article Title: CWG 2026: India’s jumpers overcome absence of regular trainers
Article Text:
Murali Sreeshankar (Image credit: PTI)

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: India’s jumpers have emerged among the standout performers in athletics at the Commonwealth Games, but their impressive results have come despite the absence of their coaches.High jumper Sarvesh Kushare clinched silver, while long jumpers Murali Sreeshankar and Lokesh Sathyanathan progressed to the final. High jumper Adarsh Ram finished fifth. Yet, throughout the competition, jumpers have largely been without their Indian coaches, who train them on a daily basis and guide them during competitions.Sarvesh’s coach Jithin Thomas is currently overseeing the Athletics Federation of India (AFI) training camp in Spala, Poland, which runs until Sept ahead of the Asian Games. Adarsh’s coach Sahana Kumari is with the Indian U-20 team for the World Athletics U-20 Championships in Eugene starting early next month. Sreeshankar’s father and coach, S Murali, a constant presence during his competitions, was not cleared to accompany him to Glasgow.The lack of dedicated coaching support became evident during the men’s high jump final. After withdrawing with a knee injury during the warm-up, Tejaswin Shankar stayed back to help Sarvesh from the sidelines.Noticing Sarvesh struggling with his approach, Tejaswin suggested a change in his run-up, advice that helped the eventual silver medallist regain rhythm. Tejaswin, himself, however, had no coach to support him through his own injury setback.According to the final athletics contingent cleared by the govt, chief coach Radhakrishnan Nair is the only Indian support staff personnel accredited with the contingent. The four foreign coaches accompanying the team are Scott Simmons (long distance), Jason Alexander Dawson (400m and relays), Ronald Gerd Weigel (race walking) and Yoandris Betanzos Francis (jumps).However, both Weigel and Betanzos have travelled as Extra Team Officials (ETOs), an accreditation that does not permit access to the competition venue and field of play. As a result, Betanzos can only watch the event from the stands and interact with athletes outside the venue, leaving India’s jumpers effectively without technical guidance during competition despite their strong performances.Raosaheb Jadhav, Sarvesh Kushare’s childhood coach, said, “Forget a coach, not a single support staff member was near the three Indian jumpers. All the other 15 jumpers had a coach or support staff member to correct their mistakes. During his two failed attempts, Sarvesh’s lower back touched the bar. Had there been a coach, he could have spotted the mistake on video and corrected it. Sarvesh could then have cleared 2.28m on his second attempt and won the gold. ”(inputs by Amit Sampat)
Article Summary: High jumper Sarvesh Kushare clinched silver, while long jumpers Murali Sreeshankar and Lokesh Sathyanathan progressed to the final. Yet, throughout the competition, jumpers have largely been without their Indian coaches, who train them on a daily basis and guide them during competitions.

Article Title: 'Bangladesh extremely safe country': BCB president Tamim Iqbal on India's Bangladesh tour in 2026

Bangladesh Cricket Board (BCB) president Tamim Iqbal remains hopeful that India will travel to Bangladesh for the scheduled white-ball series in September 2026. The six-match series, comprising three ODIs and three T20Is, is still uncertain due to several factors. However, Tamim said discussions are underway with the Board of Control for Cricket in India ( BCCI ), and the Bangladesh board is making efforts to ensure the series takes place.“Unfortunately, I don't have any news regarding the India series. I am in discussions with the BCCI and there’s an exchange of emails happening between BCB members, and we are trying from all quarters,” Tamim was quoted as saying by Cricbuzz.“Bangladesh's series against India, the excitement is at a different level, I'm sure from journalists, from fans, cricketers, everyone,” he said.India last toured Bangladesh in 2022 for a two-match Test series, where they registered a 2-0 clean sweep.The BCB president admitted that while he is working towards bringing India to Bangladesh, there are certain matters that are beyond his control.“Bangladesh is an extremely safe country, and I am very hopeful that they will come. Whatever steps need to be taken from our side, we are trying,” he added.“I am the BCB president, and there is also a line that I should never cross.So from my position, whatever is possible to do within my responsibility, I am talking to people, I am trying to tell them what advantages there are with the India series and all those things,” Tamim said.“There are certain things that are beyond my control. The discussions I've had so far have been very positive discussions. They also have to make a decision. Very soon, perhaps, we will find out whether the series is happening or not.So we will know very soon,” he added.The proposed series comes at a time when cricket ties between India and Bangladesh have faced challenges.India had decided against travelling to Bangladesh for the T20 World Cup due to security concerns during the previous government led by Muhammad Yunus. The decision had created uncertainty over future bilateral cricket engagements between the two nations.However, recent geopolitical developments have renewed hopes that India's tour of Bangladesh could go ahead as scheduled.

Former Chennai Super Kings head coach Stephen Fleming is set to take charge of England's Test team, with a report claiming the former New Zealand captain has emerged as the frontrunner to succeed Brendon McCullum in the red-ball setup. According to The Telegraph, Fleming has been identified as England's preferred candidate after a comprehensive interview process led by managing director Rob Key.The Telegraph report states that Fleming outperformed other contenders, including former England batter Jonathan Trott and current England men's performance director Richard Dawson, to secure the role. If appointed, Fleming will replace fellow New Zealander Brendon McCullum, who recently stepped down as England's Test head coach following a disappointing run of results in the longest format.Despite leaving the Test role, McCullum will remain in charge of England's white-ball teams, setting up a unique coaching partnership. The duo share a long-standing relationship, with McCullum making his Test debut under Fleming's captaincy for New Zealand. Fleming has also been regarded as one of McCullum's biggest mentors during his cricketing career, a factor the England and Wales Cricket Board (ECB) reportedly believes will help ensure smooth coordination between the two coaching units.The reported appointment comes shortly after Fleming ended his remarkable association with the Chennai Super Kings franchise. Over an 18-year stint across CSK and its sister franchises, including Texas Super Kings and Joburg Super Kings, Fleming established himself as one of franchise cricket's most successful coaches.During his time with CSK in the IPL, he guided the team to five Indian Premier League titles, helping build one of the competition's most consistent and successful dynasties.England are scheduled to host Pakistan in a three-match Test series next month. However, the report suggests former captain Joe Root is expected to lead the side on an interim basis before Fleming officially assumes charge during England's winter tour of South Africa.If confirmed, Fleming's appointment would mark one of the biggest coaching changes in world cricket, with England entrusting one of the game's most decorated tacticians to oversee their Test rebuild ahead of the 2027 Ashes.

Article Title: 'IPL isn't the only yardstick': Saransh Jain on maiden India call-up
Article Text:
Saransh Jain selected for India vs Sri Lanka test match (PTI Photo)

When Saransh Jain walked into Indore’s Shri Ranjeet Hanuman Temple on Tuesday, he had no idea that he was on the cusp of the biggest moment of his cricketing career. “After returning from the temple, my phone was inundated with messages and missed calls. I realised that I was selected in the Indian Test squad for next month’s Sri Lankan tour,” Saransh told TOI.Having spent the last decade grinding his way through the rigours of domestic cricket, far away from the glamour of franchise cricket, the call-up almost seemed like divine intervention for the Madhya Pradesh allrounder. At 33, he is the oldest to earn a maiden India Test call-up in this century.“My selection shows that the IPL alone is not the yardstick for making the cut. It is proof of the hard work I have put in domestic cricket. I would like to thank the selectors for showing faith in me,” he said.The hamstring injury to Washington Sundar gave him the opening, but he insisted that he had done enough to remain in contention. “The just-concluded India ‘A’ tour of Sri Lanka, where I picked up six wickets and scored an unbeaten 70, instilled confidence. Two years back, the six-for against Mumbai at the Irani Trophy was another important milestone,” he said.Saransh continued his stellar form in the previous Ranji Trophy season, scoring 518 runs and nabbing 30 wickets averaging a shade over 20. As an offspinner, Saransh prides himself on his craft more than mystery.“I rely on my stock ball (off-spin), topspinner and the straighter one. I am yet to develop the doosra, although I can bowl legspin with the white ball,” he said. Under Chandrakant Pandit, he added another dimension, bowling from round the wicket to right-handers, bringing LBW and both edges into play.While Ravichandran Ashwin’s versatility and videos remained a source of learning, it was an interaction with Harbhajan Singh at Bengaluru’s Centre of Excellence that left a lasting impression. “I met Bhajji about three months ago. He gave me some tips like how to use the crease better and bowl with a higher arm action because I tend to go slightly around-arm. Bowling with a more perpendicular action, he said, would help me get the desired drop,” Saransh noted.Amid the euphoria, Saransh admits that his father remains his biggest inspiration. “My father (Subodh Jain) is my hero. He was the reason why I became a cricketer,” he said. Subodh, also an off-spinner who played for MP in the 1980s, would often tell his son, “Bowl like the best off-spinner and bat like a proper No.4.”It was easier said than done. Saransh’s journey illustrates that the path to Team India can also be laid through the grind of the Ranji Trophy.
Article Summary: Saransh Jain is the oldest to earn a maiden India Test call-up in this century. The 33-year-old has spent the last decade grinding his way through the rigours of domestic cricket. The Madhya Pradesh allrounder scored 518 runs and nabbed 30 wickets last season.

Article Title: Big leadership change! Bangladesh remove Mehidy Hasan, hand ODI captaincy to Litton Das

Bangladesh have named Litton Das as their new ODI captain, handing the experienced wicketkeeper-batter the responsibility of leading the side in the 50-over format until the 2027 ICC Men's Cricket World Cup.The appointment means Litton will now captain Bangladesh in both white-ball formats, having already been in charge of the T20I team. He replaces Mehidy Hasan Miraz, who has been relieved of the ODI captaincy as the Bangladesh Cricket Board (BCB) reshapes its leadership group ahead of the next World Cup cycle.BCB president Tamim Iqbal announced Litton's appointment during a press conference in Mirpur, confirming that the board has opted for a change in ODI leadership as Bangladesh begins preparations for the 2027 World Cup. Litton has previously led the national side whenever the regular captain was unavailable and now receives the role on a full-time basis.This is his first full-time ODI captaincy assignment, Litton is no stranger to leadership. He has captained Bangladesh in seven international matches, registering three wins, three defeats and one no-result, gaining valuable experience in the role. The BCB will hope that continuity under Litton helps Bangladesh build a settled squad ahead of the 2027 World Cup.The decision marks a significant shift from the board's earlier stance. In April, the BCB had extended Mehidy Hasan Miraz's tenure as ODI captain through the 2027 World Cup while retaining Litton as T20I skipper. The latest move, however, sees Litton assume charge of both white-ball teams as Bangladesh look to chart a new direction under a single leader.Litton Das, who made his ODI debut in 2015, has established himself as one of Bangladesh's key white-ball batters. His career-best score of 176 remains one of the highest individual ODI scores by a Bangladeshi batter, and he has accumulated 2,869 runs in 104 ODIs with five centuries and 14 fifties.
Article Summary: Bangladesh name Litton Das as their new ODI captain. Das replaces Mehidy Hasan Miraz, who has been relieved of the role. Litton will now captain Bangladesh in both white-ball formats. He has already been in charge of the T20I team.

Article Title: ICC punishes Pakistan seamers after defeat against West Indies in first Test
Article Text:
ICC Penalises Pakistan duo Mohammad Abbas, Khurram Shahzad (Image: ICC)

Khurram Shahzad fined, Abbas officially reprimanded

No formal hearing required

Pakistan fast bowlers Mohammad Abbas and Khurram Shahzad have been sanctioned by the International Cricket Council (ICC) for separate breaches of the ICC Code of Conduct during the opening Test against the West Indies at the Brian Lara Cricket Academy in Tarouba. Both players were found guilty of Level 1 offences under Article 2.5, which prohibits players from using words, gestures or actions that could incite or provoke an aggressive response from a batter following a dismissal.Khurram Shahzad received a 15 per cent fine on his match fee and was handed one demerit point after celebrating too close to West Indies batter Shai Hope following his dismissal in the 17th over of the hosts' second innings. Meanwhile, Mohammad Abbas was issued an official reprimand along with one demerit point for his animated celebration after dismissing Jomel Warrican, the final wicket of the West Indies innings. The ICC ruled that both celebrations crossed the acceptable standard of player conduct and had the potential to provoke the dismissed batters.Both Abbas and Khurram accepted responsibility for their actions and agreed to the sanctions proposed by ICC Elite Panel Match Referee Jeff Crowe.As a result, the disciplinary process was concluded without the need for formal hearings. The charges were brought by on-field umpires Alex Wharf and Richard Kettleborough, along with third umpire Jayaraman Madanagopal. The ICC also confirmed that this was the first disciplinary offence for both players in the past 24 months.The West Indies won by 90 runs against Pakistan in the first Test at the Brian Lara Cricket Academy in Tarouba, Trinidad, taking a 1-0 lead in the two-match series. The historic match, the first-ever Test hosted at the venue, concluded on day four after a dominant display from the West Indies pace battery.The defeat marks Pakistan's eighth consecutive away Test loss. Pakistan will now look to level the series when the second and final Test begins at Queen's Park Oval in Port of Spain on August 2.
Article Summary: Mohammad Abbas and Khurram Shahzad fined and reprimanded by ICC. Both players found guilty of Level 1 offences under Article 2.5 of ICC Code of Conduct. West Indies won by 90 runs against Pakistan in the first Test at the Brian Lara Cricket Academy in Tarouba.

Article Title: RCB become first IPL franchise to cross $300 million in brand value
Article Text:
File Pic: RCB players celebrate with IPL trophy. (Pic credit: RCB)

‘Franchise valuations have reached new highs’

‘RCB’s fanbase intensity and connection are unparalleled’

IPL business enterprise reaches $20.6 billion



Royal Challengers Bengaluru (RCB) has cemented its status as the most valuable franchise in the Indian Premier League (IPL), becoming the first cricket team in history to breach the US$300 million brand value mark.According to global investment bank Houlihan Lokey’s 2026 IPL Brand Valuation Study, RCB retained its No. 1 ranking with a brand valuation of US$312 million (approx. Rs 2,600 crore), marking a 16% jump from US$269 million in 2025.The report highlights that RCB’s steep valuation curve reflects the compounding impact of sustained on-field performance, industry-leading fan engagement, and a digitally mature commercial ecosystem.The valuation benchmark comes on the heels of a landmark ownership transaction earlier this year, in which RCB was acquired by a consortium comprising Blackstone, Bolt Ventures, Aditya Birla Group, and Times of India Group at a reported valuation of US$1.78 billion — the most expensive single-franchise transaction in IPL history.The record valuation growth of IPL franchises reflects the league’s transformation into a globally recognised sports and entertainment asset, according to Houlihan Lokey.“Cricket’s evolution into a globally owned, institutionally backed asset class has accelerated further in 2026, with the IPL continuing to redefine the global sports landscape,” said Harsh Talikoti, Director in Houlihan Lokey’s Financial and Valuation Advisory business.“What the market confirmed this year, through landmark franchise transactions, is the extent to which the league can attract the caliber of global, institutional, and strategic capital it was built to draw. Franchise valuations have reached new highs, private capital participation has accelerated, and the league’s commercial ecosystem continues to diversify,” he added.Punjab Kings co-owner Ness Wadia highlighted how the perception of IPL franchises has evolved: “They’re no longer seen as cricket teams that play for two months every year. They’re increasingly being viewed as long-term sports and entertainment businesses.”“Centralised media rights, revenue sharing, and financial discipline have created a model that’s stable and sustainable. That gives owners the confidence to invest for the long term,” he further added.Highlighting the reasoning behind the marquee acquisition, Satyan Gajwani, co-owner of Royal Challengers Bengaluru and Chairman at Times Internet, noted the unmatched strength of the franchise's community.“We were actively engaged in the processes for both the RCB and Rajasthan Royals, and both are great assets. Across the league, however, RCB’s fanbase intensity and connection are unparalleled, which made this a special opportunity,” said Satyan Gajwani.Emphasising the long-term runway for Indian cricket as a global asset class, Gajwani added: “Overall, we are strong believers in the growth potential of cricket as a global sport, and exposure at both the media level and the IP level fits that thesis. The IPL has the attention of the NFL with a fraction of its monetization, and as Indian per-capita income grows and connected TV penetration increases, we expect monetization to match up to attention. We are very grateful to be able to work with exceptional partners on RCB, and we all believe in both the opportunity for the IPL to continue to grow, as well as for RCB to create a real global brand and fan equity.”RCB’s surge comes amid record growth for the league as a whole. The IPL’s overall business enterprise value grew 11.4% year-on-year to US$20.6 billion, while its standalone brand value rose 10.3% to US$4.3 billion.Behind RCB in the brand value rankings were Mumbai Indians at No. 2 (US$264 million; +7.9%) and Kolkata Knight Riders at No. 3 (US$245.0 million; +7.9%).The report attributed the league's overall valuation boom to growing institutional investor confidence, rapid Connected TV (CTV) adoption, and strong revenue visibility, as global capital increasingly views IPL franchises as long-term sports and entertainment powerhouses.
Article Summary: Royal Challengers Bengaluru (RCB) is the first cricket team in history to breach the US$300 million brand value mark. RCB retained its No. 1 ranking with a brand valuation of US$312 million (approx. Rs 2,600 crore), marking a 16% jump from US$269 million in 2025.

Article Title: Why Australia coach is dreaming of Ben Stokes' 'fairytale' return for one last Ashes
Article Text:
Melbourne, July 29 (IANS) Australia head coach Andrew McDonald believes attempts could be made to coax Ben Stokes out of retirement for next year’s Ashes

McDonald hopes for a fairytale Ashes comeback



New England coach could try to change his mind



Retirement followed controversy

Ben Stokes' Test career in numbers

Australia head coach Andrew McDonald believes the perfect build-up to the 2027 Ashes would be Ben Stokes making a dramatic return from Test retirement, admitting it would create a "fairytale" storyline for one of cricket's biggest rivalries.Stokes called time on his Test career earlier this year after England's home series defeat against New Zealand, bringing an end to an eventful tenure as captain. His retirement followed a controversial period that also saw him suspended for the second Test of that series before returning for the finale and announcing his decision to step away from the longest format.Speaking to SEN Radio, McDonald said the prospect of Stokes returning for one final Ashes campaign in England would be the ideal narrative ahead of the blockbuster series."The fairytale would be that he comes back out of retirement and takes on one more Ashes and builds a lot of hype on the way in. If you're looking at promoting that series, that's probably the angle that you would want, " McDonald said.McDonald added that he still believes the England all-rounder has enough left in the tank to compete at the highest level."To me, he's still got a lot of good cricket left in him. It'll be fascinating to see what happens," he added.Following Stokes' retirement, England also parted ways with Brendon McCullum as Test head coach, despite the former New Zealand captain reportedly trying to convince him to continue. McDonald feels the appointment of a new Test coach could reopen the conversation."Whoever the new head coach is may have a conversation with him. We don't know the definitive reason behind his retirement. He may have simply decided his Test journey was over, but there could also be an opportunity for someone to persuade him to return, " McDonald opined.Stokes had explained at the time that retiring from Test cricket was "the best thing for me right now," although McDonald believes there is still room for a change of heart.Stokes' decision came after a turbulent end to his England career. Following England's victory in the opening Test against New Zealand at Lord's, Stokes and teammate Gus Atkinson were suspended for the second Test after reportedly breaching the team's curfew by visiting a pub.While neither player was directly involved in an altercation that left a member of the team's security staff injured, both were disciplined by the England management.The pair returned for the final Test, with Stokes apologising to teammates before announcing that it would be his last appearance in Test cricket. Since retiring, the all-rounder has continued to play domestic one-day cricket for Durham and recently marked his return with a rapid century, suggesting he still has plenty to offer on the field.
Article Summary: Andrew McDonald believes attempts could be made to coax Ben Stokes out of retirement for next year's Ashes. Australia head coach admits it would create a "fairytale" storyline for one of cricket's biggest rivalries. Stokes called time on his Test career earlier this year after England's home series defeat against New Zealand.

Article Title: 'We wanted to make Garry Sobers proud': Roston Chase dedicates West Indies' Test win over Pakistan to legend

Seamers dominate the Test

Seales and Chanderpaul earn captain's backing

NEW DELHI: West Indies captain Roston Chase said his team's 90-run victory over Pakistan in the opening Test was a tribute to legendary all-rounder Garry Sobers, with the players determined to honour the cricket great. Sobers, widely regarded as one of the greatest all-rounders in the game's history, passed away on July 17 at the age of 89. Tuesday marked what would have been his 90th birthday.Following West Indies' victory at the Brian Lara Cricket Academy, Chase revealed that the team had spoken about Sobers before the match."We wanted to make him proud and had a chat about it before the match. I hope he is smiling down on us."Chase also thanked the fans who turned up to support the home side.“I also want to thank the Trinidad crowd for coming out and supporting us. It was not a big crowd, but it gave us enough energy and support to go out there and perform," Chase said.The win handed West Indies a 1-0 lead in the two-match Test series.West Indies entered the Pakistan series after a 1-0 Test series victory over Sri Lanka, and Chase said the team's recent performances were the result of months of hard work."I think these two teams that we've played, Sri Lanka and Pakistan, they're closer to us in the rankings.I don't want to say they're teams we should beat, but I think it's a more even contest between us."He further said, "The guys are confident and over the last few months we've been putting in some extra hard work. We had a camp as well before the Sri Lanka series and I think that really helped us become closer as a unit and also work on our weaknesses and improve our strengths as well. So I think that this is the upliftment of that practice and camp."Fast bowlers dominated throughout the match at Tarouba, with all 40 wickets falling to seam bowling. Justin Greaves starred with 5/27 in Pakistan's first innings, while Jayden Seales claimed 5/20 in the second innings. Together, they picked up 13 wickets.Greaves also produced the rare achievement of bowling five successive wicket maidens in Pakistan's first innings.Speaking about the conditions, Chase said, "I think it just goes to show that it was more friendly towards the seamers. The Pakistani spinner (Ali Usman) bowled a number of overs (13 in the first innings), he didn't get a wicket. (Jomel) Warrican bowled a few (18 across two innings), didn't get a wicket and didn't look too threatening as well. The (fast bowlers) really put the ball in the right areas and it paid off.”Chase said Greaves' disciplined bowling made the difference."I spoke to Justin about being disciplined and trying to starve the Pakistani batsmen of runs. I thought that would build the pressure, especially on a wicket where the ball was doing a lot. He got one wicket and everything just started to flow in his favour. He put the ball in the right areas."He added, "He bowled five consecutive wicket-maidens, which is a great skill to have because you're able to build pressure, stop the scoring rate and also get wickets. Usually, you're just keeping it tight and not really getting wickets, or you get wickets but the run rate might be flowing. For him to have that skill where he can do both, I think he's of great value for this team."Chase was equally pleased to see Jayden Seales return to form with a five-wicket haul."I'm very pleased for Jayden Seales as well. He's not been getting those big wicket hauls of recent, but to see him come here with that discipline, patience and have that determination to come and put on the ball in the right areas after not really having the best of times, I'm very happy for him."The West Indies skipper also defended opener Tagenarine Chanderpaul, whose slow innings of 21 and 35 attracted criticism."He's undervalued in the eyes of the public and the media. The game finished in four days, so it's not really a big issue if he bats slowly. His role is to wear down the bowlers and make it a lot easier for the batsmen coming in."He further explained, "So even if he doesn't get that big score, once he occupies the crease for at least two hours, 100 balls, 150 balls, he's done a great job of seeing off the new ball. It's not always about how fast you score or how many runs you score, especially as an opener. It's about how much time you spend at the crease and getting the bowlers tired for the rest of the team to come in and play their natural game."The second and final Test between West Indies and Pakistan will begin in Port of Spain on August 2.
Article Summary: West Indies beat Pakistan by 90 runs in opening Test at Tarouba. Captain Roston Chase hails seam bowling of Justin Greaves and Jayden Seales. Chase also defends Tagenarine Chanderpaul's slow innings. West Indies lead two-match series 1-0.

Article Title: 'Give us larger squads': Australia coach Andrew McDonald urges ICC ahead of 2027 World Cup
Article Text:
Andrew McDonald (Photo by Quinn Rooney/Getty Images)

NEW DELHI: Australia head coach Andrew McDonald has called on the International Cricket Council (ICC) to increase World Cup squad sizes from 15 to 17 players for the 2027 ODI World Cup.His comments come after the ICC introduced a new format that could see finalists play up to 15 matches, making the tournament longer and more physically demanding.McDonald believes larger squads would help teams deal with injuries and changing playing conditions, especially after Australia and New Zealand struggled with injured players during the 2023 World Cup."One of the big things from my perspective is if it's going to be your pinnacle event, what do your squad sizes look like? We had the dilemma of what it looked like having a 15-player squad for the last World Cup," McDonald said.He pointed out that players like Travis Head and Kane Williamson missed matches through injury, leaving teams with limited selection options."My push within it, any time you're playing more games in the same period of time, you don't want it to be attritional," he added. "You want the best players to be available. So, there should be a conversation around - yep, that's great, you've landed at that, okay, what about the squad sizes?"McDonald also said larger squads would help teams manage injuries during a packed international schedule and ensure the biggest stars remain available throughout the tournament."So let's carry the best players in there. Give us larger squads to be able to navigate through the early part, and then hopefully the pinnacle event has the best players playing, rather than being ruled out early on due to injury and the attritional nature of a World Cup," he further noted.He also questioned the new format, saying Associate nations may have fewer opportunities despite their recent growth in white-ball cricket."It's an interesting structure to a tournament. I think the Associate nations have probably been penalised a little bit in that," he added.
Article Summary: Andrew McDonald has called on the ICC to increase World Cup squad sizes from 15 to 17 players for the 2027 ODI World Cup. The ICC introduced a new format that could see finalists play up to 15 matches. McDonald believes larger squads would help teams deal with injuries and changing playing conditions.

Article Title: CWG 2026: Neeraj Chopra returns with unfinished business in Glasgow
Article Text:
(From right) Neeraj Chopra with Rohit Yadav and Anderson Peters in Glasgow (Image credit: Instagram)

The last time Neeraj Chopra competed at Commonwealth Games, he won gold in 2018. The next edition passed him by because of a groin injury. Now, after nearly nine months out and a return to competition only last month, the Olympic champion gets another chance to fight for the title in Glasgow.Competing at Doha Diamond League on June 19, where he had breached the 90m mark for the first time in his career last year, Chopra produced a best throw of 85.69m. It wasn’t enough for a top-three finish, but it did help him qualify for Commonwealth Games.It was well short of his personal best of 90.23m, but Chopra has sounded confident since arriving in Glasgow and is focused on reclaiming the CWG title he won in 2018.While the qualifiers are scheduled for Thursday, the final on Saturday night is unlikely to be a walk in the park as he will be up against long-time rival Arshad Nadeem, besides the likes of Anderson Peters, Julius Yego and Sri Lanka’s Rumesh Tharanga Pathirage.Nadeem hasn’t had the best of seasons this year but comes into the tournament as the defending champion after winning gold in 2022 with a throw of 90.18m. Yego, too, has struggled to hit top form in 2026 but finished third in Birmingham with an effort of 85.70m.Peters, who finished second in 2022, has, meanwhile, been in fine touch, with a best throw of 86.38m at Doha Diamond League. Australia’s Cameron McEntyre has also made big strides this year and remains just ahead of Chopra on this season’s world list.However, the biggest attraction will be Sri Lanka’s Pathirage after he unleashed a world-leading 92.62m at Rome Diamond League. Besides that, he has also registered throws of 89.37m, 89.28m and 88.68m this year, and Chopra admitted he has been impressed by the youngster.But the dark horse in the event could well be India’s Rohit Yadav. He heads into the tournament after winning gold at Inter-State Athletics Championships in Bhubaneswar with a massive throw of 87.05m. This will be his second Commonwealth Games after finishing sixth in Birmingham with a best of 82.22m.“I missed out last time, but I am going there to win a medal this time,” Yadav had said in Bhubaneswar.While Neeraj’s performances over the years have always inspired him to do better, Yadav is also taking confidence from the impressive performances of Indian athletes over the past few months.“Everyone has a lot of belief in themselves these days and they feel that they can also achieve great things,” added the 25-year-old.He, however, is confident there is no need to worry about Chopra despite his return to competition only last month. “He can produce big throws in any competition,” Yadav had said.Neeraj, though, is more focused on winning titles rather than producing big throws, and he will take the first step towards that when he competes in the qualifiers on Thursday.
Article Summary: Neeraj Chopra will compete in the men's Javelin Throw at the Commonwealth Games. The last time he competed at Commonwealth Games, he won gold in 2018. The next edition passed him by because of a groin injury. After nearly nine months out and a return to competition only last month, Chopra has sounded confident.

Article Title: From job hunt to CWG glory: Gulveer Singh's inspiring journey to silver medal
Article Text:
Gulveer Singh (Image credit: X)

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

What are you running for?” “World peace? The homeless? The environment?” The questions they asked Forrest Gump, they should have thrown at Gulveer Singh. Because, a decade ago, before living the life of an athlete, all Gulveer knew was to run. Running to help his father at the farm, running errands for his family, running to get selected in the Indian Army, so that, paradoxically, the running stops.Back in 2018, the boy from Sirsa village in Atrauli district, near Aligarh, didn’t know that running would define him a few years later.On Tuesday evening, in falling Glasgow rain, the Asian champion added a big medal to his tally by winning silver in the men’s 10000m at the Commonwealth Games. By clocking 27:49.78s, Gulveer became the first Indian to win a medal in the event, finishing behind Australia’s Ky Robinson (27:48.93s).Gulveer’s silver run completed another lap of sorts. He has joined the late Milkha Singh and Avinash Sable , both of whom won non-relay medals at the Commonwealth Games before him.Sable landed his steeplechase silver at Birmingham in 2022 while Milkha’s 440yard gold at the 1958 Cardiff Games was the country’s first medal at the Commonwealth Games.Incidentally, all of them have been athletes from the Indian Army.While Indian relay teams have won four medals (one gold, one silver and two bronze) between them, Harminder Singh (men’s 20km walk bronze, 2010) and Kavita Raut (women’s 10,000m bronze, 2010) are the other non-relay medallists for India.Even though he joined the Army to run away from running, the running never stopped for Gulveer. “After I joined the Army, I was told about sports, and that I would get a promotion if I won medals. I started running and was shifted to the Army Sports Institute in Pune, where I started to train for competition,” the Naib Subedar told TOI.Call it muscle memory or sheer talent, Gulveer adapted quickly and soon started winning inter-unit races in the army. By 2021, he was already training for national and international tournaments and won his first senior medal, a bronze at the 2022 Federation Cup.Medals at the National Games, a bronze at the Hangzhou Asian Games in 2023 followed as he started participating in the 5000m as well.Perhaps it is the intrinsic nature of his chosen sport, that in running as in life, Gulveer believes in keeping things simple. “I know that it is my job to run and I want to do my job well. All I was thinking about yesterday was how to win a medal. I was not thinking about anything else during the whole race,” he said. “I have been training in the US on and off, for many months now. It is my responsibility to train well and win medals,” he said.Asked what he likes to do when he is not running, his was a disarmingly honest reply. “I eat and sleep.”Gulveer says he owes a lot to fellow Armyman and longdistance runner, Kartik Kumar. “Whatever I know today, has been taught by Kartik bhai . He tells me everything, right from what I should eat, how I should train and run. He has been an inspiration,” Gulveer said about the Asian Games silver medallist.But beneath all that humility, there lies a competitive streak. Asked if there was any other athlete who inspired him, Gulveer offered, “I aim to become big enough to inspire others rather than aspiring to become like someone.”Gulveer has enough time to recover from the rigours of the 10,000m to be in the fray for the 5000m on Saturday.
Article Summary: Gulveer Singh won silver in the men’s 10000m at the Commonwealth Games. He is the first Indian to win a medal in the event. He has joined the late Milkha Singh and Avinash Sable in winning non-relay medals.

Article Title: CWG 2026: Murali Sreeshankar wins long jump silver; Dilip Mahadu Gavit claims Games record gold
Article Text:
India had another successful day in Glasgow as long jumper Murali Sreeshankar won his second consecutive silver medal, para athlete Dilip Mahadu Gavit claimed gold with a Games record (Image credit: Agencies)

Sreeshankar wins another silver



Dilip and Basil create history in para athletics



Indian boxers assure 10 medals



Hurdlers qualify for final



Mixed results in field events

India had another successful day at the Commonwealth Games 2026 as long jumper Murali Sreeshankar won his second consecutive silver medal, para athlete Dilip Mahadu Gavit claimed gold with a Games record, and the country's boxers guaranteed 10 medals by reaching the semifinals.With three more medals added on Wednesday, India’s overall tally reached 15 medals — three gold, nine silver and three bronze - to stay eighth in the standings.Sreeshankar continued his impressive run at the Commonwealth Games by winning silver in the men's long jump with a best effort of 8.09m. He had also finished second at the 2022 Games, becoming the first Indian to win back-to-back Commonwealth Games medals in the event.His opening jump of 8.03m put him in third place behind Scotland's Stephen McKenzie and Jamaica's Tajay Gayle, who both jumped 8.08m.Sreeshankar briefly moved into the lead with his 8.09m effort, but Gayle responded with a winning jump of 8.15m to take the gold. McKenzie settled for bronze with 8.08m, while India's Lokesh Sathyanathan finished fifth with a best jump of 7.97m.India created history in para athletics with a one-two finish in the men's 100m T47 event for athletes with upper-limb impairments.Gavit won the gold medal after clocking a Games record time of 10.71 seconds. Mohammed Basil Morssinganakathi finished second with a season-best 10.83 seconds to claim silver.It was India's third gold medal of the Games after Mirabai Chanu won the women's 48kg weightlifting title and Sharmila Dhankar claimed gold in the women's shot put F57 event.India's boxers enjoyed another outstanding day, with six more athletes reaching the semifinals and taking the country's guaranteed boxing medal tally to 10.Sakshi Chaudhary (51kg), Arundhati Choudhary (70kg), Sachin Siwach (60kg), Ankush Panghal (80kg), Narender Berwal (+90kg) and world champion Jaismine Lamboria (57kg) advanced to the last four. They joined Lovlina Borgohain (75kg), Priya Ghanghas (60kg), Preeti Pawar (54kg) and Jadumani Singh (55kg), who had already secured semifinal spots.In the final bout of the day, Jaismine defeated England's Elise Glynn 4-1 in the women's 57kg quarterfinal.The performance has already surpassed India's boxing medal haul from the 2022 Commonwealth Games, where the team won seven medals. With all 10 boxers in the semifinals, India is now assured of at least 10 bronze medals.India also had good news on the track as Yashas Palaksha and Santhosh K Tamilarasan qualified for the men's 400m hurdles final.Santhosh finished third in Heat 2 with a time of 49.51 seconds, while Yashas placed third in Heat 1 in 49.65 seconds. Both advanced as the two fastest non-automatic qualifiers.There was disappointment for Manpreet Singh, who narrowly missed a medal after finishing fourth in the women's shot put final with a best throw of 17.49m.However, Tajinderpal Singh Toor and Samardeep Singh Gill kept India's hopes alive by qualifying for the men's shot put final.Toor crossed the automatic qualification mark with a throw of 20.14m after opening with 19.93m. Gill's best throw was 19.95m, which was enough to qualify among the top 12 performers.National record holder Animesh Kujur qualified for the men's 200m semifinals after producing his season-best performance.The 23-year-old won Heat 4 in 20.46 seconds and finished seventh overall, comfortably making it to the last 16.India's campaign in weightlifting suffered a setback as Sanjana failed to finish the women's 77kg event.There was also disappointment in swimming, where Sajan Prakash and Aneesh S Gowda missed out on a place in the men's 200m freestyle final. Prakash finished 20th overall with a time of 1:51.99, while Aneesh ended 18th in 1:51.64.

Article Title: CWG 2026: Dilip Mahadu Gavit and Mohammed Basil script historic 1-2 finish for India in men's 100m T47 final
Article Text:
Dilip and Basil produce a sprint for the ages in T47 100m (Images: ESPN)

India ended the para athletics competition at the Commonwealth Games 2026 on a high as Dilip Mahadu Gavit won the gold medal with a Games record in the men's 100m T47, while compatriot Mohammed Basil Morssinganakathi claimed silver to complete a memorable Indian one-two.Gavit produced a stunning run of 10.71 seconds to break the previous Games record and finish on top of the podium. Basil clocked a season-best 10.83 seconds to secure second place, ensuring India claimed both the gold and silver medals in one of the fastest races of the competition.The gold was India's third in para athletics, with Gavit joining weightlifter Mirabai Chanu and Sharmila, who won the women's Shot Put F57 title.England's Kevin Santos took the bronze medal in 10.85 seconds, while Australia's Jaydon Page finished fourth with a time of 10.97 seconds.The result highlighted India's growing strength in para athletics, with both sprinters delivering outstanding performances in Glasgow. Gavit's Games record underlined his excellent form, while Basil's silver further boosted India's medal tally.The one-two finish took India's overall medal count to 15 at the Games, comprising three gold, nine silver and three bronze medals.Born in Toran Dongari village near Nashik in Maharashtra, Gavit grew up in a humble farming family. His life changed dramatically when he suffered a serious fall from a tree at the age of five or six, severely injuring his right arm. As timely medical treatment was unavailable, the injury developed into gangrene, forcing doctors to amputate his arm below the elbow.Despite the setback, Gavit pursued his passion for running and built a career in para athletics. He trained on the dusty roads of his village before his talent was spotted by coach Vaijnath Kale, who helped him enter professional para athletics.Gavit had earlier won gold in the men's 400m T47 event at the 2022 Asian Para Games, securing India's historic 100th medal at the continental event. He also reached the final of the men's 400m T47 at the Paris 2024 Paralympics.
Article Summary: Dilip Mahadu Gavit won the gold medal with a Games record in the men's 100m T47. His compatriot Mohammed Basil Morssinganakathi claimed silver to complete a memorable Indian one-two. The result highlighted India's growing strength in para athletics, with both sprinters delivering outstanding performances.

Glasgow: India's Murali Sreeshankar (PTI Photo/Ravi Choudhary)

Sreeshankar leads early before Gayle strikes

Gayle produces championship-winning jump

Final round ends India's Gold hopes

Lokesh Impresses on Commonwealth Games debut

India's Murali Sreeshankar clinched the silver medal in the men's long jump at the Commonwealth Games 2026, producing a best leap of 8.09m in a fiercely contested final on Thursday. The Indian star led the competition after the opening three rounds but eventually settled for silver after Jamaica's former world champion Tajay Gayle soared to 8.15m in the fourth round. Scotland's Stephen Mackenzie completed the podium with a best jump of 8.08m, just one centimetre behind Sreeshankar. The medal added another significant success to India's athletics campaign in Glasgow.Sreeshankar made an excellent start to the final, opening with a brilliant 8.09m, which kept him at the top of the standings after the first three rounds. Scotland's Mackenzie stayed within touching distance at 8.08m, while Gayle occupied third on countback despite matching the Scotsman's distance. Fellow Indian Lokesh was also in contention after recording 7.97m, sitting fourth midway through the competition.The contest took a dramatic turn in the fourth round when Gayle produced a superb leap of 8.15m to snatch the lead. Sreeshankar responded with what appeared to be a massive jump but was denied by the narrowest of margins as the attempt was ruled a foul.His father and coach, Murali, later indicated that the jump would have comfortably crossed 8.20m, highlighting just how close the Indian came to reclaiming the lead.Heading into the sixth and final round, Sreeshankar still had an opportunity to overtake Gayle. Scotland's Mackenzie, who jumped before the Indian, managed 8.06m on his final attempt, leaving his best mark at 8.08m and securing the bronze medal.Sreeshankar's final effort measured 7.97m, meaning his opening jump of 8.09m remained his best of the competition. Gayle, already assured of gold, could not improve on his last attempt but comfortably held on to the title.India's second finalist, Lokesh, enjoyed an encouraging Commonwealth Games debut by finishing fifth. Article Title: WATCH: Terrifying first-round knockout at CWG 2026 leaves boxer hanging through ropes

Terrifying knockout halts quarterfinal

A terrifying knockout at the 2026 Commonwealth Games left spectators stunned after Wales' Orlando Holley-Sotomi blasted Lesotho's Refiloe Thai through the ropes during their men's 70kg boxing quarterfinal, prompting an immediate medical response inside the ring.The frightening sequence unfolded just over a minute into the opening round when Holley-Sotomi unleashed a devastating right hand that landed flush on Thai's temple.The impact left the Lesotho boxer unable to defend himself as he collapsed through the ropes, creating one of the most dramatic and concerning moments of the Games so far.The quarterfinal had begun at a frantic pace, with both boxers looking to establish control early. Thai started aggressively, but Holley-Sotomi gradually found his rhythm and began landing clean punches.The breakthrough came quickly.A powerful right hand caught Thai on the temple, instantly taking away his balance. As the Welsh boxer followed up with a left hand, Thai collapsed through the ropes, ending up partially supported by the bottom rope while lying motionless.Medical staff rushed into the ring within seconds to attend to the injured boxer before carefully moving him back inside the ring for treatment.Thankfully, Thai soon showed encouraging signs by attempting to sit up as doctors continued their assessment, easing fears after the alarming scenes.The referee immediately waved off the contest, awarding Holley-Sotomi a first-round knockout victory.While concern remained focused on Thai's condition, the victory marked another impressive milestone for the 22-year-old Welsh boxer.Holley-Sotomi had already impressed earlier in the tournament by defeating Paddy Hewitt in his opening bout. His emphatic knockout victory now sends him into the semifinals, assuring him at least a bronze medal.Despite his eye-catching performances, the Welsh prospect insisted he is remaining grounded."I'm taking it a day at a time and taking it all in. Nobody can afford to overlook me, no-one is the favourite here," he said.The spectacular stoppage has already drawn comparisons with some of boxing's most memorable one-punch knockouts, underlining Holley-Sotomi's growing reputation as one of the breakout stars of the Glasgow Games.
Article Summary: Wales' Orlando Holley-Sotomi blasted Lesotho's Refiloe Thai through the ropes during their men's 70kg boxing quarterfinal. Medical staff rushed into the ring within seconds to attend to the injured boxer. Thai soon showed encouraging signs by attempting to sit up as doctors continued their assessment.

Article Title: Five wins, nine medals assured! India's boxing stars deliver flawless day at CWG 2026
