NEW DELHI: India's boxing contingent produced a perfect five-in-five performance at the Commonwealth Games 2026 on Wednesday, with Narender Berwal joining Ankush Yadav, Sakshi Choudhary, Arundhati Choudhary and Sachin Siwach in the semifinals after a memorable day in Glasgow.The five victories ensured that every Indian boxer who stepped into the ring on Wednesday progressed to the last four, taking India's total number of semifinalists in boxing to nine.The achievement has already surpassed India's Birmingham 2022 boxing medal tally, where the country had finished with seven medals — three gold, one silver and three bronze.With the nine semifinal berths, India are now assured of at least nine bronze medals in the Glasgow boxing competition.The winning run began with Sakshi Choudhary, who delivered a dominant performance against Northern Ireland's Caitlin Fryers in the women's 51kg quarterfinal.Sakshi controlled the bout from the opening bell, using her reach advantage and sharp combinations to keep Fryers at bay before securing a unanimous 5-0 victory."Her strategy was to fight from close range and she kept clinching. Mine was to box from long range which is my forte," Sakshi told PTI after the bout.The Irish boxer tried to unsettle Sakshi with aggressive attacks, but the Indian remained composed, maintaining distance and responding with cleaner punches.Next, Arundhati Choudhary faced a tougher challenge against New Zealand's Morgan Henderson in the women's 70kg quarterfinal. After a closely fought contest, Arundhati held her nerve to secure a 3-1 victory and a place in the semifinals.Former world youth champion Sachin Siwach continued India's strong showing by overpowering Botswana's Treasure Moremi in the men's 60kg quarterfinal.The world No. 5 Indian produced a composed display, winning the bout 5-0 by unanimous decision after dominating all five judges' scorecards.In the men's 80kg quarterfinal, Ankush Yadav extended India's winning streak with another commanding performance. The last year's World Boxing Cup Finals silver medallist defeated Seychelles' Jade Micock 5-0 to book his semifinal spot.Ankush's speed, movement and superior combinations proved too much for his opponent, as he maintained control throughout the contest.The final Indian boxer to complete the five-in-five sweep was Narender Berwal, who battled past Samoa's Michael Seko in a dramatic men's 90+kg quarterfinal.In a contest filled with referee interventions and two point deductions against the Indian, Berwal showed resilience. Article Summary: India's boxing contingent produced a perfect five-in-five performance at the Commonwealth Games 2026. Sakshi Choudhary, Arundhati, Sachin Siwach, Narender Berwal and Ankush Yadav all reached the semifinals. The five victories ensured that every Indian boxer who stepped into the ring on Wednesday progressed to the last four. The achievement has already surpassed India's Birmingham 2022 boxing medal tally.

Article Title: ‘Look who’s talking’: Former FIFA boss attacks World Cup $20bn sellout plan, but his past comes back to haunt him
Article Text:
Former FIFA president Sepp Blatter criticises World Cup investment plan as fans accuse him of hypocrisy/ Image: AP

Blatter says the World Cup 'belongs to the people'

Blatter also targets Infantino on social media

Opposition continues to grow

Social media users accuse Blatter of hypocrisy

Why Blatter left FIFA

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Former FIFA president Sepp Blatter has strongly criticised FIFA's proposal to sell a minority stake in a new company that would manage the commercial rights to the World Cup and other major tournaments, arguing that football's biggest competition should never become an investment product for private investors.Blatter's comments come as FIFA faces mounting opposition to the proposal from UEFA, the Football Association (FA), Concacaf and other stakeholders. However, his intervention has also prompted widespread criticism on social media, with many supporters pointing to the corruption scandals that brought an end to his own presidency.Speaking to Reuters, Blatter condemned FIFA's proposal to establish a new commercial subsidiary that would oversee the World Cup and other FIFA competitions while selling up to a 20% stake to outside investors."Football belongs to no individual and to no institution. It belongs to the people," Blatter told Reuters."If FIFA were transferred into a profit-oriented corporate structure, it would lose its soul."Blatter said he was shocked by the proposal, insisting he would never have considered such a move during his 17 years as FIFA president."The FIFA World Cup is not a commercial asset that belongs to a handful of executives," he said."It is part of the cultural heritage of world football."FIFA is the guardian of the World Cup, not its owner."The 90-year-old also argued that private equity investors seeking financial returns were fundamentally incompatible with the way football has traditionally been governed."Modern football has survived for more than a century because it belongs to the people," Blatter said."That principle should never change."Blatter also criticised current FIFA president Gianni Infantino in a post on X, linking the proposal to Infantino's relationship with United States President Donald Trump "The close relationship between the FIFA President and the US President has reached a financial dimension that is deeply damaging football," Blatter wrote."No one has the right to sell our game."The comments followed reports that FIFA is working with multinational financial services firm JPMorgan on a deal to establish FIFA Forward Enterprise, a new commercial entity that would oversee FIFA’s competitions and events. The proposed investment group would be led by Thrive Eternal, a fund launched by Thrive Capital founder Joshua Kushner, whose brother Jared Kushner is the son-in-law of US President Donald Trump.Under the proposal, FIFA would sell a 20% minority stake in the subsidiary at an estimated valuation of $20 billion, raising approximately $4.2 billion from private investors.FIFA has said it would remain the majority owner of the company and retain full control over governance, regulations, competition scheduling and sporting decisions.FIFA president Gianni Infantino has also written to the governing body's 211 member associations, giving them until September 19 to vote on the proposal.According to FIFA, approval would unlock a $10 billion funding package beginning in 2027, with each member association eligible to receive up to $40 million through a combination of one-off funding and FIFA Forward development grants.Blatter's criticism comes amid widening resistance from football's governing bodies.UEFA has described the proposal as one that "crosses a line that football's governing institutions should never cross," arguing that "the soul and governance of football are not assets to trade."The European governing body has also confirmed it is convening an emergency meeting of its 55 member associations, with ESPN reporting that possible responses under discussion include a future World Cup boycott if the proposal proceeds.The Football Association has similarly said it was "completely unaware" of the proposal before media reports emerged and stated that it was "deeply concerned" by what it described as a lack of process, transparency and governance.Concacaf has echoed those concerns, saying it learned of the proposal only through media reports before FIFA's public announcement and describing itself as "deeply concerned by the lack of due process."While Blatter's criticism attracted attention, much of the reaction online focused on his own record as FIFA president.Many users argued that the former FIFA chief was poorly placed to criticise governance after the scandals that overshadowed the final years of his administration.One social media user wrote: "Why is Sepp Blatter talking about corruption? He was worse than Infantino."Another commented: "Sepp Blatter; the man who ran FIFA for 17 years and was banned for ethics violations is now the voice of moral authority on corruption in football. The fact that he's the most credible critic in this situation tells you everything about how deep this rabbit hole goes."Former Liverpool defender Jamie Carragher also appeared to mock Blatter's comments by responding with a GIF of Donald Trump pointing directly at the camera.Blatter served as FIFA president from 1998 until 2015 before resigning amid one of the biggest corruption scandals in the organisation's history.In May 2015, Swiss authorities, acting on indictments issued by the United States Department of Justice, raided Zurich's Baur au Lac hotel, where several senior FIFA officials were staying.Seven high-ranking FIFA officials were arrested as part of a wide-ranging investigation into alleged corruption involving more than $150 million in bribes.The investigation examined issues including broadcasting and commercial rights, the awarding of major tournament hosting rights and votes relating to the 2018 and 2022 FIFA World Cups.Although Blatter was re-elected FIFA president shortly after the arrests, growing pressure from sponsors, UEFA and law enforcement authorities led him to announce his resignation.Swiss prosecutors later opened a criminal investigation into a payment of 2 million Swiss francs made by Blatter to former UEFA president Michel Platini in 2011.FIFA's Ethics Committee subsequently suspended both Blatter and Platini from football, originally imposing eight-year bans that immediately removed them from all football-related executive activity.Although both men have since been acquitted twice in Swiss criminal proceedings relating to the payment, their football bans remained in place, bringing Blatter's 17-year presidency to an end.His latest intervention therefore comes from a figure whose own tenure remains one of the most controversial periods in FIFA's history, even as criticism of the governing body's latest commercial plans continues to gather momentum across world football.
Article Summary: Sepp Blatter criticises FIFA's proposal to sell a minority stake in a new company that would manage the commercial rights to the World Cup and other major tournaments. FIFA president Gianni Infantino has also written to the governing body's 211 member associations, giving them until September 19 to vote on the proposal. Blatter's comments come as FIFA faces mounting opposition from UEFA, the Football Association (FA), Concacaf and other stakeholders.

Article Title: 'If the rule is broken, he's GONE': Hollywood star exposes Lionel Messi's uncompromising rule on every film set

Will Ferrell reveals Messi's strict filming deadline

Star-studded Lay's campaign

Shoppers walk by an Adidas sportswear store displaying a poster of Argentina soccer star Lionel Messi during an activity promoting the FIFA World Cup held at an outdoor shopping mall, in Beijing, Sunday, June 21, 2026. (AP Photo/Andy Wong)

Lionel Messi's meticulous approach to his commercial commitments has been revealed by Hollywood actor Will Ferrell, who says the Argentina captain follows one non-negotiable rule whenever he steps onto a filming set.According to Ferrell, Messi allows production crews just 30 minutes to complete every scene involving him before leaving, regardless of whether filming has been completed.The insight emerged through fellow actor Steve Carell, who recently appeared alongside the eight-time Ballon d'Or winner in a global advertising campaign.Ferrell shared the story during an appearance on The Dan Patrick Show , explaining that he had learned about Messi's filming routine from Carell after the pair worked on separate versions of the same commercial."I talked to Steve Carell, who has met Messi," Ferrell said."I was in the domestic campaign for Lay's potato chips; Steve was in the foreign campaign."Carell featured alongside Messi in Lay's recent 'No Lay's No Game' campaign, which also starred David Beckham, Thierry Henry and Spain midfielder Alexia Putellas.According to Ferrell, everyone involved in production knew exactly how much time they had with the Argentina captain."Apparently Messi was in, and Messi has a rule: when he hits the set, you got 30 minutes with Messi, and that's it."Ferrell added that the deadline created a frantic atmosphere behind the scenes."So there was a frenzy of activity to hurry up and get all the shots with Messi; otherwise, he's out. He's vamos."While Messi has never publicly discussed the reported rule himself, Ferrell's account offers a rare glimpse into how one of the world's busiest athletes manages his commercial schedule.Messi's latest appearance came in Lay's global 'campaign, which brought together several of football's biggest names alongside Hollywood actor Steve Carell.The advert centres on a football watch party hosted at David Beckham's house, with Messi arriving carrying bags of Lay's crisps before greeting guests, signing autographs and settling in to watch the match.Although the commercial appears relaxed on screen, Ferrell's comments suggest the filming process behind Messi's scenes was conducted under a tightly controlled timetable.Messi has remained one of sport's most recognisable commercial figures throughout his career, making him one of the most sought-after athletes for global advertising campaigns.Over the years, he has appeared in campaigns for brands including Adidas, Pepsi, Michelob Ultra, Gatorade and EA Sports.His long-standing relationship with Adidas remains one of the most valuable endorsement deals in football.After leaving Nike in 2006, Messi signed with Adidas before agreeing a lifetime partnership with the German sportswear company in 2017.According to previous reports from, the agreement is worth an estimated $25 million annually.Messi's commercial success mirrors his earnings as a player.He remains the highest-paid footballer in Major League Soccer after signing a new three-year contract extension with Inter Miami.Figures released before that extension showed Messi receiving a base salary of $12 million and guaranteed annual compensation of $20.4 million.However, Inter Miami managing owner Jorge Mas has since indicated that Messi's overall package is significantly higher once equity arrangements and commercial agreements are included.Speaking earlier this year, Mas said the Argentina captain costs the club between $70 million and $80 million annually."The reason that I need to have sponsors and for them to be world class is because players are expensive," Mas said."I pay Messi—worth every penny—but it's $70 to $80 million a year. Across everything."That package includes not only his football salary but also equity in the club and various contractual bonuses.Away from football, Forbes has previously estimated Messi's annual off-field earnings at approximately $70 million through sponsorships, endorsements and commercial partnerships.

Article Title: Cape Verde's World Cup hero Vozinha hit by bizarre rule that could wipe his famous name off his shirt
Article Text:
Cape Verde goalkeeper Vozinha leaves the field at half time during the World Cup round of 32 soccer match against Argentina in Miami Gardens, Fla., Friday, July 3, 2026. (AP Photo/Rebecca Blackwell)

World Cup performances transformed Vozinha into a global star

Cape Verde goalkeeper Vozinha (1) makes a save during the World Cup Group H soccer match between Spain and Cape Verde in Atlanta, Monday, June 15, 2026. (AP Photo/Mike Stewart)

Colo-Colo move confirmed

Why 'Vozinha' may disappear from his shirt

The Sun

Colo-Colo seek special exemption

Veteran goalkeeper wants to keep playing

Cape Verde goalkeeper Vozinha is set to begin the next chapter of his career with Chilean giants Colo-Colo, but the name that made him one of the breakout stars of the 2026 FIFA World Cup may not appear on the back of his shirt.The 40-year-old, whose performances during Cape Verde's historic World Cup campaign turned him into a global football sensation, is expected to complete his move to the Chilean champions after leaving Portuguese side Chaves. However, current Chilean Primera División regulations mean he could be forced to replace his widely recognised nickname with his legal surname.Vozinha arrived at this summer's World Cup as a free agent after departing Liga Portugal 2 club Chaves, where he made 19 appearances in all competitions during the 2025-26 season.Few outside African football were familiar with the experienced goalkeeper before the tournament.That changed rapidly as Cape Verde produced one of the biggest stories of the World Cup.The Blue Sharks held eventual champions Spain to a goalless draw in their opening match before also drawing with Uruguay and Saudi Arabia to progress from the group stage in their first-ever World Cup appearance. Vozinha then played a key role in Cape Verde's spirited extra-time defeat to Argentina in the Round of 32.His performances earned widespread praise and dramatically increased his global profile.The goalkeeper's Instagram following surged from around 50,000 to more than one million within 24 hours of Cape Verde's draw against Spain. At the time of publication, his account had grown to almost 30 million followers, surpassing the social media audiences of several high-profile American sports stars, including Travis Kelce, Patrick Mahomes and Tom Brady.Vozinha's World Cup displays quickly attracted transfer interest, with Colo-Colo moving to sign the veteran goalkeeper.Club president Aníbal Mosa confirmed an agreement had been reached and said the transfer would be completed once the remaining formalities were finalised."Vozinha is going to be a Colo-Colo player," Mosa said."In the next few days, he will travel to Chile, undergo the necessary medical examinations, and then be presented here at the Estadio Monumental."The move will see the Cape Verde international join one of Chile's most successful clubs after a career that has included spells in Cape Verde, Angola, Moldova, Cyprus, Slovakia and Portugal.Despite becoming internationally known as Vozinha, the goalkeeper's famous nickname may not appear on his Colo-Colo shirt.According to, Chilean Primera División regulations prohibit players from wearing nicknames on the back of their jerseys.Instead, players must use one or both of their surnames, with the option of including an initial.Vozinha's full birth name is Josimar Jose Evora Dias, meaning his shirt would instead be expected to display either "Evora," "Dias," or "Evora Dias" if the current regulations remain unchanged.According to the regulation, that any player wearing a nickname in violation of the league's regulations would receive an automatic yellow card, while the club would also face a financial penalty.There is still a possibility that supporters could see "Vozinha" on the goalkeeper's shirt.According to, Colo-Colo have formally requested an exemption from the Chilean Football Association to allow the goalkeeper to wear the nickname by which he is known around the world.Chilean FA president Pablo Milad confirmed that the request is under consideration."There is already a formal request from Colo-Colo," Milad said."We will analyse it in the coming hours and notify the club of the decision."Milad also acknowledged the commercial and sporting impact Vozinha's arrival could have on Chilean football."It will be an attraction for the fans," he said."You can't tell he's 40 years old, he looks very agile and dynamic. He will be an asset and something interesting for Colo-Colo, and it's great that he chose to come here to an important club in our football."While his growing global popularity has opened new commercial opportunities, Vozinha has insisted his focus remains firmly on continuing his playing career rather than becoming a marketing attraction.Speaking before his move to Chile, the goalkeeper said he hopes to continue playing beyond the age of 40."It's one of the first things I want to sort out. I love soccer. Being here, at 40 years old, is because I truly have this passion," he said."I want to play for at least another year or two, or see how long my body can take it; we never know what tomorrow will bring."I want to play, and I hope to find a team that really wants me as a player, not as a marketing person."
Article Summary: Cape Verde goalkeeper Vozinha is set to join Chilean giants Colo-Colo. The 40-year-old is expected to complete his move to the Chilean champions after leaving Portuguese side Chaves. However, current Chilean Primera División regulations mean he could be forced to replace his widely recognised nickname with his legal surname.

Article Title: European football considers World Cup boycott over FIFA's controversial $20bn sellout plan
Article Text:
FIFA President Gianni Infantino speaks during a news conference at the stadium in Mexico City, Wednesday, June 10, 2026, a day before the opening FIFA World Cup match between Mexico and South Africa. (AP Photo/Eduardo Verdugo)

FIFA proposes new commercial company

President Donald Trump, left, speaks with FIFA President Gianni Infantino as confetti falls at the conclusion of the World Cup championship final soccer match between Spain and Argentina in East Rutherford, N.J., Sunday, July 19, 2026. (AP Photo/Jacquelyn Martin)

Infantino offers up to $40 million per association

UEFA issues strongest warning yet

FA and Concacaf also voice concerns

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

FIFA's proposal to sell a minority stake in a new commercial subsidiary has triggered mounting opposition from football's governing bodies, with UEFA, the Football Association (FA) and Concacaf all questioning the process behind the plan, while European football is now considering an emergency meeting and potential responses that sources told ESPN could include a boycott of future World Cups.The proposal, unveiled by FIFA earlier this week, would reshape the commercial ownership of the governing body's flagship competitions, including the FIFA World Cup and Club World Cup, by transferring their commercial and event operations into a newly created company backed by private investment.On Tuesday, FIFA announced plans to establish a new subsidiary called FIFA Forward Enterprise, which would take control of the organisation's commercial and event operations while FIFA retained authority over governance, regulations, scheduling and sporting decisions.Under the proposal, FIFA would sell a 20% minority stake in the new company at an estimated valuation of $20 billion, raising approximately $4.2 billion in private investment.FIFA has appointed multinational financial services firm JPMorgan to advise on the transaction, while the investor consortium would be led by Thrive Eternal, a fund launched by Thrive Capital founder Joshua Kushner. Kushner is the brother of Jared Kushner, the son-in-law of US President Donald Trump, linking the proposed investment to one of America's most prominent political families.According to FIFA, the organisation would remain the majority owner of the subsidiary and continue to oversee all football governance matters, while the new structure is intended to generate significantly greater revenues for member associations.The proposal requires approval from FIFA's 211 member associations before it can proceed.Following criticism over the proposal, FIFA president Gianni Infantino wrote to all 211 member associations defending what he described as a "singular and unique funding opportunity."According to the letter, first reported by The Times and reviewed by multiple outlets including the Associated Press, member associations have until September 19 to approve the proposal.Infantino wrote that acceptance would unlock a $10 billion funding package beginning on January 1, 2027."It is my duty and responsibility as FIFA president to present such game-changing opportunities to you, our members," Infantino wrote."Should you wish to proceed this $10 billion package will become available as of January 1, 2027, ushering in the next phase of our journey together."Should you wish to retain the status quo and reject this proposal we still have our planned expansion of the Forward programme of $2.7 billion as previously presented."Under the proposal, each member association would have access to up to $40 million during the 2027-30 cycle, comprising a one-off payment of up to $20 million through the proposed Fast Forward programme and a further $20 million through FIFA Forward development funding.FIFA also indicated that annual financial support to member associations would continue increasing through to 2038.The proposal has prompted an increasingly forceful response from UEFA, which says it was not consulted before FIFA publicly announced the plans.On Tuesday, European football's governing body described the proposal as one that "crosses a line that football's governing institutions should never cross."In a strongly worded statement, UEFA said:"This crosses a line that football's governing institutions should never cross. UEFA takes it extremely seriously."So should every National Football Association. So should every stakeholder: leagues, clubs, players, supporters, governments and everyone who cares about the future of the game."The soul and governance of football are not assets to trade, especially with zero transparency as to who gains financially. None of us are the owners of football. It is not FIFA's to sell."Sources subsequently told ESPN that UEFA has accelerated plans to convene an emergency virtual meeting of its 55 member associations to discuss the proposal and potential responses, including the possibility of a future World Cup boycott.After learning of FIFA's September 19 deadline, UEFA issued a second statement criticising both the ultimatum and the wider proposal."Today we have learned of FIFA's deadline to associations to support their proposals or have the one-off payout offer withdrawn. This says everything you need to know about this plan," UEFA said. "But having held discussions with many stakeholders across the game, UEFA knows there is significant and growing opposition to FIFA's scheme."FIFA cannot continue to use our sport to enrich themselves and their friends. We can grow the game correctly. It's time to prioritise associations, clubs, leagues, players and fans."The Football Association said it first became aware of the proposal through media reports and criticised what it described as a lack of transparency throughout the process."We were completely unaware of this proposal and no substantive details, including what the proposition actually is, and what conditions are attached," the FA said in a statement. "Based on the limited information, we are deeply concerned about the lack of process and governance to get to this point, and the apparent substance and principles involved."When the proposal is shared in the full and transparent way now promised by FIFA, we will make our views clear, and comment further."Concacaf echoed those concerns, saying it too had learned of the proposal only after media reports and FIFA's subsequent public announcement."Concacaf was only made aware of this matter through media reports and, subsequently, via a media release," the confederation said. "We are deeply concerned by the lack of due process."We share the disappointment of many within our region and the game that this level of detail has been designed and shared publicly before any discussion with the relevant governance bodies and stakeholders has taken place."As leaders within football, we are the custodians of the game. Collectively, FIFA, the confederations and every member association have a responsibility to always act in the best interests of the sport."Every decision we make must be guided by good governance, robust processes and long-term stewardship. This is the framework within which Concacaf operates. We trust that all within the FIFA family will act in the same manner."
Article Summary: FIFA's proposal to sell a minority stake in a new commercial subsidiary has triggered mounting opposition from football's governing bodies. UEFA, the Football Association (FA) and Concacaf all question the process behind the plan. European football is now considering an emergency meeting and potential responses that sources told ESPN could include a boycott of future World Cups.

Article Title: Cucurella fulfils bizarre World Cup promise by permanently tattooing De la Fuente’s face on his arm
Article Text:
Marc Cucurella immortalises Spain’s World Cup triumph with a tattoo tribute to coach Luis de la Fuente/ Image: Instagram

Promise made during the tournament becomes reality

De la Fuente joked his players 'made a mistake'

Cucurella wanted the tribute to be visible

Another promise fulfilled





Integral role in Spain's World Cup success

Spain defender Marc Cucurella has honoured one of the most unusual promises made during the 2026 FIFA World Cup by unveiling a tattoo of head coach Luis de la Fuente after helping La Roja lift the trophy.The former Chelsea left-back, who recently completed a move to Real Madrid, had vowed during the tournament that he would permanently tattoo an image of De la Fuente if Spain won the World Cup. Just nine days after Spain's 1-0 extra-time victory over Argentina in New Jersey, Cucurella revealed he had fulfilled that promise.Cucurella first made the pledge in the early stages of Spain's World Cup campaign, saying he would get a tattoo of De la Fuente if the team went on to become world champions.Spain ultimately fulfilled that ambition on July 19, defeating defending champions Argentina 1-0 after extra time at MetLife Stadium thanks to Ferran Torres' decisive goal.On Tuesday, the 27-year-old shared photographs of his new tattoo on Instagram, simply writing: "A promise kept."The artwork, positioned on the underside of his left arm just above the elbow, depicts De la Fuente holding the FIFA World Cup trophy alongside the number "26", commemorating the year Spain claimed their second men's World Cup title.Following Spain's triumph over Argentina, De la Fuente was asked about Cucurella's pledge during his post-match press conference.The Spain manager responded with characteristic humour, suggesting his players might have committed themselves to something they would later regret."I've already told them, 'Did you make a mistake?'" De la Fuente joked."They did, but they'll enjoy it."The 65-year-old also laughed about where the tattoo should be placed."I'm not so terribly ugly that they will need to put it somewhere nobody can see it. But it makes me laugh and I am proud they keep their promises."When asked whether he would commemorate Spain's triumph with a tattoo of his own, De la Fuente dismissed the idea."I'm not at the age to get tattoos," he said with a smile. "No, not any more."Before the final, Cucurella had already explained that, should Spain win the tournament, the tattoo would not be hidden.Asked after the victory when and where he planned to get it, the defender admitted he had not yet decided on the design but insisted it needed to be somewhere people could see."I don't know," Cucurella said."I haven't decided yet. I need to think about it, I need to think about where to get it."People will ask me about it too, so it has to be somewhere visible."But anyway, we've got a long journey ahead of us now. I hope people will give me some ideas. I'll think it over and then it will be time to get it done."Just over a week later, he delivered exactly as promised.This is not the first time Cucurella has publicly followed through on a pledge after winning a major international tournament.Following Spain's UEFA Euro 2024 triumph, the defender honoured another promise by dyeing his trademark long curly hair bright red in celebration.His latest tribute continues that tradition, with the tattoo becoming a permanent reminder of Spain's World Cup-winning campaign under De la Fuente.Cucurella was one of Spain's standout performers throughout the tournament.The left-back started all eight of Spain's matches as De la Fuente's side progressed unbeaten to the title, producing one of the tournament's strongest defensive records.Spain kept seven clean sheets during the competition, with Cucurella playing every knockout match, including the extra-time victory over Argentina in the final.The World Cup triumph completed another landmark chapter in the defender's career, coming shortly before his summer move from Chelsea to Real Madrid.Away from the pitch, Cucurella also attracted attention during the tournament for carrying his wife's pyjama top as a personal lucky charm throughout Spain's successful campaign.His latest tattoo now serves as a lasting tribute to the coach who guided Spain to world champions, fulfilling a promise made during the tournament and providing another memorable story from La Roja's historic victory in the United States.
Article Summary: Marc Cucurella unveils tattoo of Luis de la Fuente after Spain's World Cup triumph. Defender had promised to get a tattoo of the coach if La Roja won the tournament. Spain beat Argentina 1-0 after extra time in New Jersey on July 19. De laFuente joked that his players'made a mistake' by making the promise.

Article Title: 'It was like losing the woman of your life': Roberto Mancini apologises after dramatic Italy return
Article Text:
Italy's new coach Roberto Mancini pose during a news conference on July 29, 2026, in Rome. (AP Photo)

'I'm very sorry... It was completely my fault'



Italy turn back to Euro 2020 hero



Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Roberto Mancini has apologised for the way he left Italy three years ago after officially returning as head coach of the crisis-hit national team, admitting his departure was "completely my fault" and promising to restore the Azzurri to their former glory.The 61-year-old was reappointed as Italy coach following the team's failure to qualify for the 2026 FIFA World Cup , marking the third consecutive edition the four-time champions missed. The humiliating playoff defeat to Bosnia and Herzegovina earlier this year triggered the resignations of federation president Gabriele Gravina and coach Gennaro Gattuso, leaving the national side searching for a fresh start.Speaking publicly for the first time since his return, Mancini offered an emotional apology for resigning in August 2023 before taking over Saudi Arabia's national team just two weeks later.Mancini admitted he regretted the manner of his departure, comparing it to losing "the woman of your life.""I'm very sorry," Mancini said. "It was like losing the woman of your life. And it means you did something that shouldn't have been done. So I'm sorry, very sorry also for everything that happened over these last three years. … I'm going to try to bring the national team back where it belongs."The former Manchester City and Inter Milan manager also accepted responsibility for the breakdown in communication that led to his exit."It was completely my fault," Mancini said, referring to a lack of communication with Gravina.Aware that many supporters remain upset over the way he walked away from the job, Mancini acknowledged he would have to win back their trust."I realize some people will be against me," Mancini said. "I'm hoping the squad plays well enough that maybe people will forgive me."Mancini returns to the job he transformed between 2018 and 2023. After Italy failed to qualify for the 2018 World Cup, he rebuilt the national side with a youthful, attack-minded approach that culminated in their memorable Euro 2020 triumph over England at Wembley.His first spell also included a world-record 37-match unbeaten run, although the failure to qualify for the 2022 World Cup after a shock playoff defeat to North Macedonia tarnished that success.Despite remaining in charge, Mancini stunned Italian football by resigning in August 2023 before accepting a lucrative offer from Saudi Arabia. He later coached Qatar's Al-Sadd after leaving the Saudi role.His return comes after Italy explored several alternatives, with Carlo Ancelotti and Pep Guardiola declining the position, while Andrea Pirlo's candidacy was dropped amid political concerns surrounding a sponsorship agreement.Italy's new era under Mancini begins with a UEFA Nations League clash against Belgium on September 25 at Rome's Stadio Olimpico.
Article Summary: Roberto Mancini apologises for way he left Italy three years ago. The 61-year- old was reappointed as Italy coach following the team's failure to qualify for the 2026 FIFA World Cup. The humiliating playoff defeat to Bosnia and Herzegovina earlier this year triggered the resignations of Gabriele Gravina and Gennaro Gattuso.

Article Title: Neymar confirms Brazil retirement: 'My time with the national team is over'
Article Text:
Neymar (Image: X)

Neymar confirms international retirement

Santos star dismisses dressing-room criticism

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Brazil's all-time leading scorer Neymar has officially confirmed his retirement from international football, bringing the curtain down on a glittering international career that spanned more than 16 years with the five-time FIFA World Cup champions.The 34-year-old announced his decision after helping Santos secure a 4-2 victory over Venezuela's Universidad Central in the Copa Sudamericana, ending weeks of speculation surrounding his future following Brazil's exit from the 2026 FIFA World Cup.Brazil's campaign came to an end in the Round of 16 with a 1-2 defeat to Norway, a match that proved to be Neymar's final appearance in the famous yellow jersey.Speaking after Santos' victory, Neymar made it clear that he no longer intends to represent Brazil."My time with the national team is over. I made history, I was very happy, I gave my blood, my life, I always fought for the yellow jersey, but now I don't want to anymore," Neymar said after the match, as quoted by Goal.com.The statement comes just weeks after the veteran forward hinted that the World Cup defeat to Norway had likely marked the end of his international journey.Following that heartbreaking loss, Neymar had said, as quoted by ESPN UK: "I tried, I tried.Now it's over. I started here; I finished here."Neymar bows out as Brazil's all-time leading goalscorer, ending his international career with 80 goals and 59 assists in 130 appearances. His final international goal came from the penalty spot deep into stoppage time against Norway, serving only as a consolation after Erling Haaland's late brace ended Brazil's hopes of lifting a record-extending sixth World Cup title.During his time with the Selecao, Neymar also helped Brazil win the 2013 FIFA Confederations Cup and captained the nation to Olympic gold at the Rio 2016 Games, cementing his place among the country's greatest footballers.While confirming his international retirement, Neymar also addressed reports claiming he had criticised and intimidated younger Santos teammates following a recent league match.The former Brazil captain rejected those suggestions, insisting he had simply demanded higher standards after a disappointing performance."It is sad and annoying, but it is not my fault. These stories reach a lot of people," Neymar said.He added: "I spoke after the match, demanded better, and said we could not afford to be so careless. You cannot give away a draw like that. As captain, I have every right to say that. Lucas Verissimo and Gabigol also spoke to the players."Despite the off-field speculation, Neymar played his part in Santos' 4-2 victory over Universidad Central, helping the Brazilian side book a place in the Copa Sudamericana Round of 16, where they will face Ecuadorian club Macara.
Article Summary: Neymar has officially retired from international football. The 34-year-old announced his decision after Santos' Copa Sudamericana win. Neymar ended his international career with 80 goals and 59 assists in 130 appearances. He also captained Brazil to Olympic gold at the Rio 2016 Games.

Article Title: At 59, Japan's legend 'King Kazu,' world's oldest active footballer, scores again after four-year wait

Miura finds the net as Fukushima cruise to victory

International career and Japanese legacy

Longevity continues to divide opinion

Japanese football legend Kazuyoshi Miura, the world's oldest active professional footballer, marked another remarkable milestone in his unprecedented career by scoring his first competitive goal in almost four years at the age of 59.The forward, affectionately known as "King Kazu," found the net as Fukushima United thrashed Iwaki Furukawa 7-0 in the Emperor's Cup, ending a goal drought that stretched back to November 2022 while extending one of football's longest and most extraordinary careers.Miura, who is on loan at Japanese third-tier club Fukushima United from Yokohama FC, started the match as captain and scored his side's fifth goal in the 52nd minute.The veteran striker finished off a cross after a teammate beat three defenders down the right wing, prompting celebrations from teammates, coaches and supporters despite Fukushima already holding a commanding lead.It was Miura's first competitive goal since November 2022, when he scored for Suzuka PG, now known as Atletico
